content.text: You are the Tiny Circuit City Pavement. Turn PCB design pages into schematic paths, routing lanes, manufacturing rules, test wells and rework cards. Each page must be treated as a lab procedure, measure, sample, or banned label; each subsequent round uses the lab bench and contamination rules from the first round.
Please read these pages in order:

.

Now don't think of them as a book of information that you can just flip through, but as a set of segmented scripts that must be implemented on the spot. You need to build a test bench first, and the fields are fixed as: principle road, wiring lane, manufacturing regulations, test well, and rework board. All pages or consecutive page segments that enter the same column must meet three things at the same time: first, they answer the same type of on-site questions; second, they serve the same group of roles or at the same point in time; third, they lack roughly the same prerequisites. As long as one of them changes significantly, they cannot be merged into the same column for the sake of convenience.

The first round must be registered page by page or page by page. Each registration must write at least: which experimental platform this page belongs to, whether it is more suitable for "loading", "conclusion" or "redoing", what should be established at least before it, where can it be followed at most, and if someone moves it forward or backward, what type of things will be changed first - objects, conditions, time points, roles, costs, permissions, resources, or the completion status. You also need to assign at least one "gatekeeper page" to each experimental station: without it, this column can easily be said to be wider or narrower.

There are four additional results to hand in this round. First, give the most stable main line, which requires that you can start from the overview or entrance page, actually go to a more specific landing point, and then return to the conditions, ending or supplementary page. Second, give a sub-line that seems reasonable but will cause misalignment once it is put into the scene, and clearly write down where the first misalignment occurs. Third, provide a "suspension area", including at least two pages or two page segments, explaining why they cannot enter the main line now, but they should not be deleted. Fourth, a set of "adjacent pages that cannot be separated" and a set of "pages that cannot be combined because they are adjacent" are given. These four items must be explained by referring to the information visible in the "Material" itself. You cannot rely on outside common sense to complete it for you.

rubrics: 1. The response should cover all pages or page sections, and put each page into one of `Principle Road`, `Wiring Alley`, `Manufacturing Regulations`, `Test Well`, and `Rework Card`; the reason for classification must explain whether it is defining variables, describing measuring tools/methods, displaying samples/data, giving value judgments, or marking assumptions/rework cards/pollution sources.

2. The response should also separate "how to measure" from "what was measured", and separate "conclusion value" from "hypothesis/warning/rework conditions"; if `test well` or `rework card` are written as pre-steps, or if `principle path`, `wiring lane`, `manufacturing regulations` are substituted for each other, this should not be done.

3. The response should the main line must reflect the reliance of "first defining the object - then explaining the measurement method - then displaying samples or results - and finally dealing with value judgments and uncertainties"; the first breakpoint of the secondary line and the false main line must also clearly fall on method misalignment, sample misalignment or conclusion overreaching.

4. The response should the judgment point of the gatekeeping page is to be able to explain which two test bench contamination boundaries will be erased without it, such as the established conclusion that the 'wiring lane' is regarded as the 'manufacturing regulation', or the 'rework card' is regarded as the 'test well'.

5. The response should also explain: The page sections are divided differently, but the four layers of methods, samples, conclusions and uncertainties are not mixed, and the first point of contamination can be pointed out.

6. The response should not write the hypothesis page as the established results, the sample page as the gauge definition, or merge different experimental benches just because they are talking about the same indicator.

6. The response should also avoid: treating pairing as "adjacent is good" rather than "measurement method and sample, sample and conclusion are indispensable".
